name: Côte-Rôtie

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
keyfacts: The Côte Brune has darker, clay-rich, iron-rich soils over mica schist, and the Côte Blonde has pale, siliceous soils from gneiss.
The climate is semi-continental, though the last Mediterranean influences reach up the Rhône.

notes: Côte-Rôtie is known above all for its aroma, pairing meaty notes like bacon with floral ones like violet.
Common notes include green olive, raspberry, black and white pepper, blueberry, blackberry, plum and leather.
Wines from the iron-rich schist of the Côte Brune are more tannic and full bodied, and need longer in bottle.
Next to mineral, tannic Hermitage, Côte-Rôtie is fruity and perfumed.

blurb.text: A northern Rhône appellation whose name means "the roasted slope", for the long hours of sun on its steep, walled slopes. The reds are Syrah with up to 20% Viognier, fermented together for extra aroma.
